prior_importants.description: For chore and refactor, `Scope boundary` is marked `area: true`. Both the form and the rubric ask that field to name what the change leaves alone, so paths the ticket stays out of fire the module-boundary and ADR-area triggers.

When the area names a file by its GitHub permalink, the extracted path starts with `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<ref>/`. That path matches no ADR glob and no module, so `adr-area` and `module-boundary` don't fire and the design gate passes when it should fail.

The chore/refactor, docs and spike headings in the code don't match the labels in the repo's issue forms. Every form-filed chore, refactor, docs or spike ticket reports a required field as missing, and intake would strip `ready` from even a fully filled ticket.

A directory-style area such as `src/cli/ and src/core/` (the form-placeholder style) yields no module and no ADR match, so a bug or chore that crosses modules or touches an ADR area gets `needsDesign: false`.

A `# comment` line inside a fenced code block is read as a heading and splits the section there. A shell comment in a reproduction or area block can make a filled field vague, or drop its paths so the design triggers don't fire.

findings.description: moduleOf's new rule (no extension in the last segment means a directory) treats a test-helper path ending in a sentence period, or a wildcard under test/<kind>/, as a module. That gives a false module-boundary trigger and a design the ticket doesn't need.
findings.body:
**A false `module-boundary` from the new directory rule in `moduleOf`**

```ts
const directories = /\.\w+$/.test(parts.at(-1) ?? '') ? parts.length - 1 : parts.length;
if (parts[0] === 'test' && directories > 2) return parts[2];
```

The last segment of `PATH` (line 95) is `[\w.*-]+`, so it keeps a period that ends a sentence and it matches `*`. Neither passes the `/\.\w+$/` extension test, so the new rule counts that segment as a directory. Under `test/<kind>/` that makes `directories` 3, and the file name or the wildcard comes back as a module:

- **Bug:** `Suspected area` is `The bug is in src/core/land.service.ts and its mock test/helpers/land.mock.ts.`
  - `PATH` yields `test/helpers/land.mock.ts.` and `moduleOf` returns `'land.mock.ts.'`.
  - The modules are `{core, land.mock.ts.}`, so `module-boundary` fires and `needsDesign` is `true`.
- **Chore:** `Files in scope` is `src/core/land.service.ts, test/helpers/*`. The modules are `{core, '*'}`, with the same result.
- **Bare source file:** `src/index.ts.` now returns `'index.ts.'`.

At 5eb4df85 these paths had only 3 parts (2 for `src/index.ts.`), so they failed the old `parts.length > 3` / `> 2` checks, returned `undefined`, and fired nothing. This commit introduced the regression. `test/helpers/` is a real directory of `*.mock.ts` files and is not a `test/<kind>/<module>` folder. Area fields are free text, so a sentence that ends in a path is ordinary input.

**Fix:** treat an extension followed by an optional period as a file, and treat any segment with a `*` in it as a file glob.
- `src/core/**` still gives `core`.
- `test/helpers/*.` and `test/helpers/land*` give `undefined`.
- Every path in the current tests keeps its module.

A test to pin it: a bug with `Suspected area` set to `src/core/land.service.ts and test/helpers/land.mock.ts.` expects `triggers: []`.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/c6972069753379843cf91959184b44101e5e2ef4/src/core/ticket-intake.utils.ts#L153-L159>

findings.description: `closesFence` has a single caller, the `else if` in `sections()`. It carries a second fence regex (`/^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})\s*$/`) that largely repeats `FENCE_OPEN`. Inlining it as `const m = /^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})\s*$/.exec(line)?.[1]; if (m && m[0] === fence[0] && m.length >= fence.length) fence = undefined;` removes the helper and its 5-line JSDoc. Its WHY comment, 'same character, at least as long, nothing after', would stay on the inline form. A second caller would justify keeping it, but none exists today. This is a judgment call, since the helper is small and named.
